To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
global information systems (IS) is an area of research that has evolved from a focus on domestic U.S. perspectives to a more internationally oriented focus.

the five elements of Global Information Systems are: (1) the organization, which is a collection of individuals, departments, and business units that are organized to accomplish a specific task; (2) the client, who is the person or organization who receives the information system; (3) the market, which is the group of people or organizations who are the target for the information system; and (4) the system, which is the collection of components, which are organized to accomplish the task; and
the Global Information Systems are a key element in the success of global organizations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the management of Global IS and the impact of Global IS on organizations.
how Global IS is being used to support the global strategies of organizations.
the challenges and opportunities of Global IS and the implications for organizations in a global environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Global IS framework can help organizations to better understand the challenges in the development of Global IS, which can be used to develop strategies and plans for Global IS.
Global IS can be viewed as a network of interrelated information systems, which support a global organization in the global marketplace.

the Global IS are an important component of the global business strategy and that the five elements of the Global IS framework are the key components to address and link the Global IS to the global business strategy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Global IS are the information systems that connect the organization with its clients, market, system and network/platforms in a global environment.
the Global IS is a complex and dynamic environment, which requires a strategic and integrated approach.
the Global IS is an organizational strategy, a network of systems, and an infrastructure of information.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Global IS must be viewed as a holistic system and that the five elements are interrelated.
Global IS is a dynamic and complex phenomenon that is not easily captured by a single model or a single perspective.
Global IS must be viewed as a complex system of interacting elements that are interdependent, and therefore, the Global IS strategy must consider the interdependencies among these elements.
